anomalies.observed: The ATO solenoid-valve low-side switch (reference T6 in the build) is populated as an AO3400A (small SOT-23-class 30 V N-MOSFET, ~5.7 A). The only AON6407 on the sheet is T7, used in the 24 V input reverse-polarity-protection position, not on the valve.
anomalies.expected: The specification assigns the AON6407 (8-DFN, much larger die) to the ATO-valve low-side switch: 'T3 — AON6407 (8-DFN N-MOSFET) | ATO solenoid-valve low-side switch | Netlist: drives ATO_VALVE net; gate driven through R10 (100 Ω), pre-driven via T4 (BT3904).' The ATO-valve switch should therefore be the AON6407, not the AO3400A.

evidence.quote: T3 — AON6407 (8-DFN N-MOSFET) | ATO solenoid-valve low-side switch ... Netlist: drives ATO_VALVE net

"ATO Valve" section of sheet 1 (Main Pump & Valve Drivers): T6 / AO3400A with gate resistor R5 100 Ω and BT3904 pre-driver T2, driving the valve load; the AON6407 device appears only as T7 in the input protection block.

anomalies.impact: If the solenoid valve (or its inrush) exceeds the AO3400A's rating, or if the intended 8-DFN footprint was used, the ATO valve driver will overheat/fail or be mis-assembled, so automatic top-off will not behave as designed. (The same substitution also moves the AON6407 into the input path.)

parsed.summary: The schematic largely matches the specification, but the ATO solenoid-valve low-side switch is drawn as an AO3400A rather than the AON6407 the specification assigns to that function (the AON6407 instead appears in the 24 V input reverse-polarity position), a component substitution that can change or break ATO-valve drive behaviour.
